paint.intro: Brush over what came out wrong, then remesh again: painted areas get smaller quads.
paint.tooltip: Brush over the parts that came out wrong -- a rim, a strap, a buckle -- in the Scene view, on the result or on the source, then press Remesh again: painted areas get smaller quads (up to 3x finer) and the target grows by what they add. Less Detail paints the other way.

size.label: Brush Size %
size.tooltip: Radius, as a percentage of the object's size.

strength.label: Strength
strength.tooltip: How much one pass adds. Strokes add up to full strength.

paint.help: Drag on the mesh in the Scene view. Shift erases, Ctrl paints Less Detail, Esc stops. Alt still orbits.

typeNotes: Each part is read on its own, from its shape: sculpted, modelled or scanned.
Sculpted or organic: fingers and toes get rows of quads, straps and belts become tubes.
Modelled: clean-quad parts keep their own loops, panel lines become loops, tread and grilles go to the normal map.
Photogrammetry or a laser scan: noise is not taken for edges, walls and columns get rows along them.

fields.name: roundParts
fields.label: Rings on turned parts, rows on extruded ones
fields.tooltip: Any kind. A piece a rotation sweeps -- a tyre, a rim, a disc, a bottle, a knob -- gets its quads in rings round its axis and rows along it; one an extrusion sweeps, in rows along it. Found by fitting the motion that slides the piece along itself.

fields.name: characterSourceLoops
fields.label: Clean quads keep their own loops
fields.tooltip: A model that already is clean quads (retopologised, modelled) is reduced by taking out whole edge rings, so its own loops and poles stay, instead of being remeshed.

fields.name: characterStraps
fields.label: Straps and belts as tubes
fields.tooltip: Thin straps, belts and cords get clean tubes of quads round them.

fields.name: characterThinRows
fields.label: Rows across fingers and toes
fields.tooltip: Parts thinner than a few quads (fingers, toes, ears' rims) get quads across them, with the count raised to pay for it, instead of being flattened.

fields.name: hardSourceLoops
fields.label: Clean quads keep their own loops
fields.tooltip: A modelled part that already is clean quads (a car's panels) is reduced by taking out whole edge rings: its lips, flanges and panel edges stay its own. Parts that will not reduce cleanly (a tyre's tread at a few hundred quads) are remeshed.

fields.name: hardDenseToNormalMap
fields.label: Dense edges to the normal map
fields.tooltip: Sharp edges packed close (tread, grilles, vents) are left to the normal map; edges standing apart (panel lines) become edge loops.

fields.name: hardThinStrips
fields.label: Two quads across thin strips
fields.tooltip: Open strips narrower than a quad (pillar trims, flanges) get two quads across.

fields.name: hardRods
fields.label: Quads round thin rods
fields.tooltip: Rods thinner than a few quads (pipes, handrails, a mirror's arm, a barrel) get quads round them, with the count raised to pay for it, instead of being dropped and leaving what they hold in the air.

fields.name: hardMergeFlat
fields.label: Big quads on flat plates
fields.tooltip: On a dense model of plates, quads are merged where that costs no shape: a flat plate takes a few large quads, the parts keep theirs, and the count drops.

fields.name: hardEvenRows
fields.label: Even rows at the count
fields.tooltip: The quads are laid once, in even rows, at the count asked: the count is not raised for curved ground and the rows are not merged back down afterwards. Off: more quads on curves, then merged where flat. Faster, but on the cars, the house and the armoured car it leaves more folded and bent faces than the merging, so it is off by default.

fields.name: hardAcrossRounding
fields.label: Edges found across their rounding
fields.tooltip: An edge rounded over several triangles (a window frame, a door gap, a wheel arch) is measured across its rounding, so the rows follow it. Off: edge by edge, with the dense and the flat panels' tests (the default: sharper plates on the armoured car).

fields.name: hardFlatPanels
fields.label: Flatten panels
fields.tooltip: The output's faces are faired at the end: where neighbouring faces nearly agree they are made to agree, so ripples in the source smaller than a quad (and the solve mesh's streaks) leave the panels flat instead of crumpled; the normal map carries them. Edges between panels stay sharp. Off: the points stay on the source as laid.

fields.name: hardEdgesAtCount
fields.label: Small details to the normal map
fields.tooltip: Each edge is checked on the source at the size of a quad of the count asked: at a low count a door handle, a door's gap or a seam does not bend the rows and is left to the normal map, while window frames, sills and arches stay edges. At a higher count the smaller edges come back. Off: every edge found is kept at any count.

fields.name: hardToCount
fields.label: Merge down to the count (low poly)
fields.tooltip: Keep merging until the result has the count asked, even where it costs shape: edges, rods and parts are kept before the round surfaces, which turn faceted.

fields.name: hardPlateRows
fields.label: Plates in rows
fields.tooltip: Before the merging, quads on a flat plate are merged nine at a time into rows of big quads that follow the plate's edges, with a ring of steps round them, and kept so.

fields.name: hardRowsAtMerged
fields.label: Even rows at the merged count
fields.tooltip: The quads are laid again in even rows at the count the merging came to, and not merged: the same faces, the doors and roofs flat instead of crumpled by the big merged quads. Takes a second solve. Off: the merged quads.

fields.name: hardShapeRegions
fields.label: Rings and rows inside parts too
fields.tooltip: Inside a piece, regions that are round (turned) or straight (extruded) get rings or rows along their shape.

fields.name: scanShapeRegions
fields.label: Rows along walls and columns
fields.tooltip: Walls, columns and other straight or turned regions of the scan get rows or rings along their shape (ccnb at 5000: worst distance 0.0169 -> 0.0135).

fields.name: targetQuadCount
fields.label: Quads
fields.tooltip: How many quads to make. With curves adding theirs, this sizes the quads on flat ground and curved areas add more on top.

fields.name: curveDetail
fields.label: Smaller quads on curves
fields.tooltip: How much smaller quads get where the surface curves, in percent -- and, when curves add quads, how many they add. 0 is an even grid everywhere; higher spends more on fingers, rims and folds.

fields.name: curvesAddQuads
fields.label: Curves add quads
fields.tooltip: Curved areas get their smaller quads on top of the count, up to 3x it (5000 asked gives 11,000-14,000 on a character).

fields.name: longCreaseLoops
fields.label: Along long creases
fields.tooltip: Creases that run as long clean lines (grooves, seams) get edge loops along them; short creases from scan noise are ignored. Matters on scans; Hard Surface finds its creases either way.

fields.name: symmetry
fields.label: Mirrored
fields.tooltip: One half is remeshed and mirrored in X, Y or Z, welded along the plane, so both sides get the same edge loops. The plane is the object's local origin when the mesh straddles it, else the middle of its bounds. Clean-quad models are then remeshed rather than reduced by their own loops.

fields.name: materialBorders
fields.label: On material borders
fields.tooltip: The borders between the mesh's materials (submeshes) become edge loops, and the result keeps one submesh per material, with the source's materials on it.

fields.name: bakeTexture
fields.label: Its texture
fields.tooltip: Give the result its own UV layout and bake the source's texture into it, with a material using it. The source's own UVs would otherwise be carried over, and on a scan, whose texture atlas is cut into thousands of pieces, about half the quads straddle a cut and show a smeared strip. Reads the texture file at full size.

fields.name: bakeNormalMap
fields.label: Its surface detail, as a normal map
fields.tooltip: Bake the source's surface detail into a tangent-space normal map over the result's own UV layout, with a material using it: what the quads are too coarse to carry -- slots, screws, seams, folds, a tire's tread -- comes back as shading, the way game assets are made. Needs no source texture.

fields.name: textureSize
fields.label: Size
fields.tooltip: Width and height of both baked textures. Auto: the source texture's own size, read from its file (the largest, with several), so an 8K scan bakes at 8K; 4096 when there is no source texture.
